name: Wilderness Road State Park
dates: Park year round, fort weekends May–October
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: A reconstructed 1775 frontier fort called Martin's Station on the road Daniel Boone widened into the Wilderness Road, staffed by interpreters in period clothing who demonstrate blacksmithing, militia drill and open hearth cooking at the edge of the Cumberland Gap.
buzz: The fort weekends are the reason to time a visit, and the interpreters stay in character without being precious about it. The park also has a trail along the old road bed.

name: White Rocks and Sand Cave via the Ewing Trail
unique: An eight mile climb from a valley trailhead to a sandstone cliff line on the Kentucky border, with Sand Cave, an overhang big enough to hold a house and a floor of loose sand, and a ridge walk to White Rocks with a view across three states.
buzz: The cave is the payoff and the climb is the price. Hikers warn that the last pitch is steep and that the sand floor is cold even in summer, and everyone says start early.

name: Trail of the Lonesome Pine Outdoor Drama
customer: Theatre people, families, Appalachian history fans
unique: The official outdoor drama of Virginia, staged since 1963 in an amphitheater cut into the mountain above Big Stone Gap, telling the story of the feuding families and the coal boom that turned a valley town into a company town.
buzz: Volunteers build the sets and the cast comes back year after year. Locals bring blankets and picnic before the show, and the mountain backdrop does half the work.

name: Southwest Virginia Museum
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
customer: History people, families, coal country researchers
unique: A rambling 1895 Victorian mansion built by a coal and iron speculator, now a state museum of the coalfields with rooms of mining tools, company scrip, furniture and photographs of the boom towns that grew and emptied within a lifetime.
buzz: The house itself is the surprise in a town of this size, and the mining collection is more personal than institutional. Staff are happy to talk about specific camps.

name: Guest River Gorge Trail
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: A rail trail on the old Norfolk and Western grade along the Guest River, running through three tunnels and over trestles above a gorge with sandstone cliffs, roughly five and a half miles one way and almost flat the whole way.
buzz: The tunnels and the river access are what people come for, and the flat grade makes it the walk locals recommend to anyone who does not want a climb. Watch for falling rock signs.

name: High Knob Tower
dates: Forest road open April–November, gate closed in winter
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
customer: View chasers, hang glider pilots, photographers
unique: A forest observation tower at 4,223 feet on the high point of the Cumberland plateau, with a platform that shows five states on a clear day and a launch ramp used by hang glider pilots who ride the ridge lift.
buzz: The drive up is steep and the gate closes in winter, which people learn the hard way. On a clear morning the view is the best in southwest Virginia.

name: Clinch River State Park
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: Virginia's first blueway state park, a string of riverfront parcels along the Clinch connected by canoe access rather than roads, with the Sugar Hill unit at St. Paul open for hiking and biking above the water.
buzz: Paddlers treat the Clinch as the best smallmouth bass river in the state and the park is built around putting in and taking out. Facilities are still being built, so expect portable toilets and rough parking.

name: Breaks Interstate Park
unique: The deepest gorge east of the Mississippi, a sixteen hundred foot cut in the Cumberland plateau that straddles the Virginia and Kentucky line, with overlooks on both rims, a lake, and whitewater releases on the Russell Fork in fall.
buzz: The Grand Canyon of the South nickname undersells the fall rafting, which runs Class IV and V releases a few weekends a year and sells out. The overlooks are a short walk from the parking lots.

name: Ralph Stanley Museum
company: Ralph Stanley Museum and Traditional Mountain Music Center
customer: Bluegrass fans, musicians, Appalachian history people
unique: A museum to the Clinch Mountain Boys founder and his brother Carter, in a century old house on Clintwood's main street, with Stanley's instruments, stage clothes, recordings and a listening room where the mountaintop removal of the old time sound is explained track by track.
buzz: Fans make pilgrimages and leave saying the listening stations are the best part. The staff will talk about the Bristol sessions and the Stanley family for as long as you let them.

name: John W. Flannagan Dam and Reservoir
unique: A Corps of Engineers flood control lake of eleven hundred acres in a mountain hollow, with a campground, a beach, a marina and bass fishing that local anglers rate among the best in the coalfields.
buzz: Quiet and cheap compared with the state parks, and the campground fills on summer weekends. The dam and spillway are worth the walk.

name: Southern Gap Outdoor Adventure
customer: ATV riders, elk watchers, camping families
unique: A county built trailhead on a reclaimed mine site at the base of the Spearhead Trails network, with cabins and RV sites, ATV and side by side rentals, and guided elk tours into the herd that was reintroduced to these mountains after a century and a half.
buzz: Riders come for the hundred miles of trail and stay two days. The elk tours are the surprise, and sightings are common at dawn on the grassland the mine left behind.

name: Virginia Elk Viewing Tours
dates: September and October, booked in advance
unique: Guided bus tours into the elk restoration zone in Buchanan County, run by state wildlife biologists during the fall rut, when bulls bugle across the reclaimed mine grasslands and the herd that was reintroduced in 2012 is now large enough to see in a morning.
buzz: Tours sell out quickly and people report dozens of animals on a good morning. The guides explain the reintroduction and the arguments around it rather than just pointing.

name: Bootlegger's Run
customer: Motorcyclists, sports car drivers, history curious
unique: A mapped driving route out of Grundy that follows the ridge roads and hollows used by moonshiners running liquor to West Virginia, with waypoints on the old still sites, river crossings and switchbacks that made the route hard to patrol.
buzz: Drivers describe it as the quiet alternative to the famous motorcycle roads, with almost no traffic and some very rough pavement. The history panels are the part people did not expect.

name: Pinnacle Natural Area Preserve
company: Virginia Department of Conservation and Recreation
unique: A limestone gorge where Big Cedar Creek drops through a series of falls into the Clinch River, with a trail along the water, cliffs used by nesting ravens and a great blue heron rookery downstream.
buzz: The falls and the heron rookery are the draws, and the trail is short enough for a half day. Spring wildflowers are the local secret.

name: Honaker Redbud Festival
customer: Local families, craft vendors, car show crowds
unique: A spring festival timed to the redbud bloom on the hills around a small Russell County town, with a parade, crafts, a car show and music, and hillsides that turn pink for about ten days a year.
buzz: Locals say the bloom is the real attraction and the festival is the excuse. It is small, free and entirely local.

name: Elk Garden Trail
dates: Year round, road may close in winter
company: George Washington and Jefferson National Forests
customer: Hikers, Appalachian Trail section hikers, photographers
unique: A high saddle at 4,200 feet where the Appalachian Trail crosses from Russell County into the Mount Rogers high country, with open balds, a spruce forest and a day use area that puts wild ponies and the state's highest ground within a few miles.
buzz: Section hikers use it as a start or finish and day hikers use it for the balds. The gravel road up is the usual complaint.

name: Burke's Garden
dates: Year round, best June and October
unique: An eight mile wide bowl in the top of a mountain, farmed since the 1740s by families who still work the bottom land, seen whole from the rim road where the valley floor lies a thousand feet below and the fields run to the base of the encircling ridge.
buzz: Called God's Thumbprint by locals and photographed from the overlook on Route 623. Drivers are asked to stay on the road and respect that every acre is somebody's farm.

name: Historic Crab Orchard Museum and Pioneer Park
unique: A museum of the Virginia frontier with fourteen original log and stone buildings moved to the site, including a cabin, a barn, a blacksmith shop and a one room school, plus galleries on the Cherokee presence and the first settlers in the valley.
buzz: The pioneer village is the part kids like and the collection inside is better than a county museum has any right to be. Volunteers demonstrate crafts on event days.

name: Back of the Dragon
unique: Thirty two miles of Virginia Route 16 between Marion and Tazewell with more than three hundred curves, climbing over three mountains and dropping into the Clinch valley, promoted by the county as a riding road with a welcome center at each end.
buzz: Riders come from several states and rate it as technical rather than fast, with blind switchbacks and gravel in the turns. Weekdays are quiet and weekends bring groups.
